note: SAME DEPOSIT AND SAME METHOD AS batch_202's gilbert_meta_73, so the reasoning there applies here too. Live codes are the dictionary's variable names with the wave prefix stripped, and the live `wave` column (0 baseline, 0.5 midline, 1 endline) carries what the prefix encoded. The renaming happened upstream of this repo -- data/gilbert_hte/postprocessing.R points at an external 'gilbert_share/06 IL-HTE Econ/analysis/' -- so the correspondence was verified against the data rather than read off a script. ITEM TEXT IS THE TASK DESCRIPTION, NOT A LITERAL ITEM, and that is deliberate rather than a gap: the deposit ships FOUR parallel forms whose content differs, and the live table records no form, so no literal item is a property of an item code. The visible consequence is that item_text repeats across a task family. resp is 0/1 and the deposit publishes no value labels for these variables, so option_text is blank; that 1 means correct follows from makedata.do recoding 9 to 0 and summing the items into test scores, and is recorded in the public note as an inference rather than a transcription. VERIFICATION: 12 of the 33 codes are wave-restricted by the dictionary and all 12 hold in the data -- the nine baseline-only codes (comp1-comp4 comprehension, and the six let_fill boxes) appear at wave 0 alone, and the three endline-only word_dic codes appear at 0.5 and 1 only. The remaining 21 span all three waves as the dictionary implies. That the baseline and endline forms differ in content is itself the finding: the baseline form carried comprehension and letter-filling tasks that the endline forms dropped, and the endline forms added word dictation. A NOTE ON WHAT THESE ITEMS ARE: several are picture-dependent -- matpic ('Encircle the word which matches with the picture'), obj_name ('Look at the picture and write the name of the object') and writpic ('Look at the picture, and write the word') -- so even with a single form there would be no transcribable stem beyond the task, only an image. The task description is the whole of the available text for those nine items regardless of the parallel-forms problem. TWELVE OF THE THIRTY-THREE ITEMS NOW CARRY REAL TEXT. Corrected 2026-09-14, same correction as gilbert_meta_71 in this batch. The first version shipped the dictionary's task label ('Comprehension') for all 33 items on the parallel-forms argument, without opening the booklets -- which were cached the whole time. The deposit publishes ALL of them: four baseline forms (Written test .Baseline./Hindi_Written_1-2/Hindi1-2_Form1..4.pdf) and four endline samples (FBT and written test .Endline 1 and 2./Written Std1-2/mit1-2 sample 1..4.pdf). Reading them shows some positions print different content on each form and others print the same content on every one. WHAT GAINED TEXT, AND WHY EACH: the four comprehension items (comp1-4) ship their question and all three options, and their section_prompt carries the full rabbit-and-ant passage they depend on -- without it 'What was the rabbit like?' is unanswerable. com_sen1 and com_sen3 ship a sentence-completion stem with its three options. matpic3 and matpic4 ship their three word options with item_text BLANK, because the item itself is a picture (scissors, a kite) and only the options are words. let_fill2_1/2_2 and let_fill3_1/3_2 ship the letter sequence they complete; the two codes in each pair are the first and second blank of one sequence, which is what the dictionary's qno (2.2.1/2.2.2, 2.3.1/2.3.2) encodes, so both carry the same sequence. WHAT STAYS BLANK, AND THE THREE DIFFERENT REASONS: (a) the position prints different content on each form -- let_fill1, matpic1-2, com_sen2, make_sen*; (b) the item IS a picture with no printed words at all -- writpic*, obj_name*; (c) the item is dictated aloud by the enumerator and never printed in the child's booklet -- let_dic*, word_dic*. Only (a) is the parallel-forms problem; (b) falls under the 2026-09-05 picture-stimulus ruling and (c) is simply not a printed item. The first version collapsed all three into one undifferentiated task label. HOW CONSTANCY IS TESTED. verify_gilbert_meta_70.R part B reads the booklets and records, per position, how many contain a distinctive substring of its printed content, taken from the PDFs' own text layer. Those files use a legacy Kruti-Dev encoding that extracts as transliterated noise, but the noise is DETERMINISTIC, so identical content gives identical strings. All 14 tested positions agree with the shipped reading, and unlike gilbert_meta_71's arithmetic every position here discriminates, because Hindi words are long enough not to collide. Codes the dictionary defines at baseline only (let_fill*, comp*) are checked against the four baseline forms, which is their complete set. LANGUAGE. language=Hindi, with the instrument's printed Hindi in section_prompt, item_text and option_text, and English in the matching _translated columns. The Hindi was transcribed from pages rendered at 150 dpi, not from the text layer, for the encoding reason above -- which is precisely why the first pass never saw any of this. The English is IRW's translation, not the study's; the deposit supplies an English rendering for the standard 3-5 Hindi form but not for 1-2. correct_response is empty throughout: the deposit publishes no key for the written tests. For the comprehension items the answer is recoverable from the passage by any Hindi reader, but deriving one would make it IRW-generated content owing an issues-page line, and that was not worth doing for four items. option_text rows carry no resp, because resp is a 0/1 accuracy score and without a key no option maps to it; each item also carries its two scored levels on their own rows, the shape used for 13code in gilbert_meta_23. COLUMN LAYOUT AND TRANSLATION COVERAGE, fixed 2026-09-14 after the user read the shipped file: each _translated column now sits immediately after the field it translates (section_prompt / section_prompt_translated, item_text / item_text_translated, option_text / option_text_translated) rather than being bunched at the end. In the first layout the three translated columns sat at positions 11-13 while their bases were at 6, 7 and 9, so a row with a blank item_text and a populated section_prompt_translated read as an English translation of nothing. Nothing in the data was wrong; the order made it unreadable. Every base/translation pair is now complete in both directions: no populated field lacks its translation and no translation exists without its base. DICTATION SHEET, found 2026-09-14 when the user pointed back at the deposit. 'Written test .Baseline./Hindi_Written_1-2/Dictation for Stds1-2.pdf' is the enumerator's sheet and lists the four letters read aloud for EACH of the four baseline forms: छ/ख/न/ध (form 1), ग/ख/ल/ध (2), झ/ख/प/ध (3), म/ख/ह/ध (4). So dictation positions 2 (ख) and 4 (ध) are the same letter on every baseline form and positions 1 and 3 are not. THOSE TWO STILL SHIP BLANK: let_dic is defined in all three waves and the deposit publishes no endline dictation list -- the endline booklets print only answer blanks at प्र.1 -- so constancy across waves cannot be established and shipping the baseline letter would be wrong for endline rows. The letters are recorded here because they are real recovered content and should not have to be found a third time. WHAT THE SHEET DID FIX: the two sections that had no prompt now have the instrument's own spoken instruction. Section 1 (let_dic) is 'सुनो और अक्षर लिखो।' / 'Listen and write the letter.', which appears on all four baseline dictation panels and at प्र.1 of all four endline booklets; section 9 (word_dic) is 'सुनो और शब्द लिखो।' / 'Listen and write the word.', at प्र.2 of all four endline booklets, which is the complete set for a code defined at endline only. All nine sections now carry a prompt. ALSO CHECKED AND EMPTY: the deposit's variable workbook RawTestVariables_UTK_BH.xlsx has an 'Answer Details' column that the first extraction ignored. It is populated for the ASER and FBT sheets but blank for every std 1-2 written-test row, so it adds nothing here. OPTION ROWS NOW CARRY raw_resp, 2026-09-18, and the first version was defective -- same fix as gilbert_meta_112, same reason. It shipped 24 option rows across 8 items with no resp, no raw_resp and no correct_response, so nothing joined them, alongside 16 score-level rows carrying only the item code. red_up rejected the table on dup_item_resp. THE RULE APPLIED: an option row must carry resp or raw_resp; both blank is a defect. Each option row now carries its own Hindi wording in raw_resp, which makes the options addressable and turns the score rows into the residual rather than padding. THE VALUE IS THE WORDING BECAUSE THE BOOKLET NUMBERS NOTHING. Rendering Hindi1-2_Form1.pdf at 120-150 dpi shows bare checkboxes beside each option -- no letters, no numbers -- so a letter code would be IRW-invented. gilbert_meta_11 uses letters because its own booklet prints them and its correct_response speaks that vocabulary; there is no correct_response here, so the wording is the handle. option_text keeps the same string, each field true to its own definition. NO KEY EXISTS, CHECKED THREE WAYS AND ALL THREE ARE DEAD ENDS. (1) The deposit's own scoring workbook, RawTestVariables_UTK_BH.xlsx, has an 'Answer Details' column and it is EMPTY for all eleven std12 items -- matpic1-4, com_sen1-3, comp1-4. (2) makedata.do only rowtotals variables that were already scored 0/1; there is no option-to-correct recode anywhere in it, so the scoring was applied before deposit. (3) The response data records accuracy only, never the chosen option, so no key can be solved from responses. SIX OF THE EIGHT ARE IN PRINCIPLE DERIVABLE AND WERE DELIBERATELY NOT DERIVED: the comprehension passage prints directly above its questions, so a Hindi reader can see that the rabbit was आलसी and was resting पेड़ के नीचे. Deriving those would make IRW the author of the key, which owes a public issues-page line under the 2026-09-03 ruling, and provenance_vocab.csv has no key_source value for a key read off a printed stimulus -- derived_from_responses would be false here. Not worth six items without a ruling; raised with Ben instead. matpic3/matpic4 depend on pictures and are not derivable at all.

VERIFICATION AND A SOURCE ERROR IT FOUND. The wave test is weak on this table -- 19 of its 20 codes are defined in all three waves, so only one code is discriminating -- and that one code exposed a TYPO IN THE DICTIONARY rather than a problem with the mapping. mathwrit_std12_add2d_b is listed with b_ and e2_ prefixes but no e1_, which would mean it was not administered at midline; the data has it at midline. The cause is visible in the sheet: 'Math Aser & Written test-End1' row 8b gives the variable name as e1_mathwrit_std12_add2d_a, duplicating row 8a, while that row's own question label correctly reads 'q8_b Addition-two digit'. It cannot affect what ships: rows 8a and 8b carry the identical task description, 'Addition-two digit'. EIGHT OF THE TWENTY ITEMS CARRY THE REAL QUESTION; TWELVE CARRY NOTHING. Corrected 2026-09-14. The first version shipped the dictionary's task label ('Addition-one digit') for all twenty items, on the argument that four parallel forms mean no literal item belongs to a code. That argument is sound for most positions and wrong for the rest, and it was applied without opening the booklets -- which were in the cache the whole time. THE DEPOSIT PUBLISHES EVERY FORM: four baseline booklets (Written test .Baseline./Math_Written_1-2/Maths 1-2_Form1..4.pdf, with an English rendering of Form 1 alongside) and four endline booklets (FBT and written test .Endline 1 and 2./Written Std1-2/mit1-2 sample 1..4.pdf). Reading all eight shows that some question positions print a DIFFERENT problem on each form -- position 4a is 4+6, 7+5, 3+6, 6+2 across the baseline forms -- while others print the SAME problem in all eight. The eight constant ones now ship their literal question: miss_no_b (99 ___ 101), add1d_c (12 + 8), add1d_d (9 + 9 + 9), subt1d_a (8 - 3), nm_name (16), num (अठारह), subt2d_b (75 - 62), subt2d_d (31 - 13). HOW THE CONSTANCY CLAIM IS TESTED, AND WHERE THE TEST RUNS OUT. verify_gilbert_meta_71.R part B reads all eight booklet PDFs and counts, per position, how many contain every operand of that position's problem: a fixed problem appears in 8/8, a varying one does not. Ten positions have at least one two-digit operand and are therefore discriminating; all ten agree with the shipped reading (constants 8/8, variables 2/8 or 4/8). Five positions have only single-digit operands, which appear somewhere on every math page, so the count is uninformative for them -- add1d_d and subt1d_a are shipped constant on the evidence of the rendered pages instead, as is num, whose content is the Hindi word अठारह rather than a numeral. That limit is stated in the script's own output rather than hidden. LANGUAGE. The instrument is in Hindi and the table now says so: language=Hindi, with the instrument's own Hindi question instructions in section_prompt and English in section_prompt_translated. The nine sections are the nine printed questions. Only one item_text needs translating -- num, अठारह / eighteen -- because every other constant item is an arithmetic expression in Western numerals, which is what the booklets print. The Hindi was transcribed from pages rendered at 165 dpi, NOT from the PDF text layer: these files use a legacy Kruti-Dev-style encoding that extracts as transliterated noise ('gy djksA' for हल करो), which is exactly why the first pass never saw the items. Numerals extract correctly, which is what makes the programmatic constancy check possible. ONE WORDING DIFFERENCE BETWEEN WAVES, DISCLOSED: question 6's instruction reads 'नीचे दिए गए संख्या को शब्दों में लिखो।' on the baseline forms and 'नीचे दिए गए संख्या को हिन्दी में लिखो।' on the endline ones. The item (16) is identical, so it ships; section_prompt carries the baseline wording. correct_response is empty throughout: the deposit publishes no answer key for the written tests, and IRW has not derived one. option_text is empty because resp is a 0/1 accuracy score. COLUMN LAYOUT AND TRANSLATION COVERAGE, fixed 2026-09-14 after the user read the shipped file. Two changes. (1) Each _translated column now follows the field it translates instead of sitting at the end. (2) EVERY item that carries item_text now carries item_text_translated, including the arithmetic. The first version left the translation blank for the seven numeral items on the reasoning that '12 + 8' needs no translating, which is true of the string and false of the reader: a user who does not read Hindi goes to item_text_translated and found it empty for precisely the items that were readable. The numeral items now repeat the expression there, which is what their English rendering is, and num gives 'eighteen' for अठारह. Complete in both directions.

note: THIS IS THE HARYANA ARM, a different state from gilbert_meta_70/71/73, and that matters for provenance. haryana_analysis.dta labels these variables with the QUESTION NUMBER only -- 'Written Hindi 1.1', 'Written Math 1a' -- not the task, so the wording is bridged from the study's own UTK/BH dictionary by question number. THAT BRIDGE IS THE TABLE'S ONE INFERENCE and it is recorded as such: no Haryana test instrument is deposited (the deposit's test folder is explicitly 'Bihar and Uttarakhand'), so this rests on Haryana having used the same printed forms. The evidence that it did is strong rather than assumed -- the question-number sets correspond exactly and idiosyncratically, and two different instruments would not share that structure. Live codes are the variable names with the h_/m_/base_ prefixes stripped, which is why waves 0 and 1 share one code set and every code appears at both. A CONSEQUENCE: the wave availability route that verified gilbert_meta_70/71/73 has no discriminating power here, so difficulty clustering was used instead -- see the verify script. ITEM TEXT IS THE TASK DESCRIPTION, not a literal item, for the same reason as the other Banerjee tables: four parallel forms and no form recorded in the live table. resp is 0/1 with no published value labels, so option_text is blank; 1 means correct on the evidence of the deposit's own scoring code, recorded as an inference. The Hindi correspondence is a straight dot-to-underscore transform: dictionary 1.1 through 11.2b maps to q1_1 through q11_2b, 35 codes matching 35 exactly. Worth knowing about the content: several families are picture-dependent or productive tasks ('Look at the picture and make a sentence', 'Word dictation'), so even with a single form there would be no transcribable stem beyond the task. ITEM TEXT IS THE TASK LABEL AND STAYS THAT WAY, BUT FOR A REASON THAT CAN NOW BE SHOWN RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Revisited 2026-09-14 alongside gilbert_meta_70/71, where opening the deposit's booklets let most of a blanket 'parallel forms' claim be replaced with real questions. The same was attempted here and FAILED, for a specific and documented reason worth recording so nobody repeats the attempt. THE HARYANA INSTRUMENT IS DEPOSITED, LEGIBLE, AND INCOMPLETE. questionnaires/tests/Haryana/RI Written 1.pdf is the written test: 14 pages, scanned, with NO text layer -- which is why the first pass never saw it; rendered at 150 dpi it is perfectly readable. Its section headers are the problem. The reading half is titled 'पढ़ने का टेस्ट (1)' and the mathematics half 'गणित लिखित सेम्पल (1)' -- literally 'Math written SAMPLE (1)'. So this is one of a set of parallel samples, exactly as in the Bihar/Uttarakhand arm, and the deposit contains only the first. For that arm the deposit ships all four forms plus four endline samples, which is what made the constancy test in gilbert_meta_70/71 possible; here there is nothing to compare sample 1 against, and the live table records no sample. Shipping sample 1's wording would therefore attribute it to children who sat samples 2, 3 or 4 -- the same error as the pooled forms in gilbert_meta_13/14. WHAT SAMPLE 1 CONTAINS, recorded so the reconnaissance is not repeated: the questions are fully transcribable and map cleanly onto the dictionary's qno positions. Reading: प्र.4 'चित्र देखो, शब्द पूरा करो।' with picture-plus-partial-word items (त__जू for तराजू, क__म for कलम); प्र.5 'अब यह चित्र देखो, चित्र का नाम लिखो।' (umbrella, elephant); प्र.7 'सही शब्द पर घेरा (O) लगाओ और खाली जगह में लिखकर वाक्य पूरा करो।' with 'मुझे किताब ____ ।' (दिखाओ / खिलाओ / पिलाओ) and 'हम अपने ____ से सुनते हैं।' (कानों / नाक / आँखों); प्र.8 'शब्द लिखो और वाक्य पूरा करो।'. Mathematics: प्र.1 'गिनो और सही संख्या पर घेरा (O) लगाओ।'; प्र.2 'खाली डिब्बे में जो छूटा हुआ है उसे लिखो।' (7 _ 9 and 99 _ 101); प्र.3 'इनमें से 9740 का संख्यानाम कौनसा है?' with four options. A SUGGESTIVE CROSS-ARM DETAIL, NOT PROOF: several of these are the SAME items as the Bihar/Uttarakhand forms -- 99 _ 101 and 'मुझे किताब ____' with the identical three options both appear there and are constant across all eight of that arm's booklets. That raises the odds that they are constant across the Haryana samples too, but the other Haryana samples are not published, so it stays an inference and nothing ships on it. TO CLOSE THIS: obtain Haryana samples 2-4 (they are not in the deposit; author contact or the Haryana state evaluation records), then run the same constancy test used in verify_gilbert_meta_70.R part B. language=Hindi is now set. item_text remains the study's own English task label from the variable dictionary, which is a description rather than administered wording, so it has no _translated twin -- the administered wording is the Hindi in sample 1 and is deliberately not shipped.

note: ITEM TEXT IS A LITERAL TRANSCRIPTION FROM PAGE IMAGES, AND THE IMAGES ARE WHY THIS TOOK CARE. The deposit's item document is 11 JPEGs inside a .docx with no extractable text layer, so every stem and option was read off the images. Two deliberate limits on what got transcribed. First, NOTHING IRW WROTE IS IN item_text: where an item's stem refers to a picture ('How many birds are shown below?', 'Which picture represents twenty-three?') the words are transcribed and the picture is NOT described, per the 2026-09-05 picture-stimulus ruling. Where the response OPTIONS are pictures rather than text -- items 10, 11 and 23 -- no options are listed at all, so those three item_texts are stems only. Second, on-screen numeric material that is genuinely part of the item (count sequences, fact families, the lists of draggable numbers, the grid in item 6) IS transcribed, linearised into running text because a CSV cell cannot hold a grid. That linearisation is the one transformation applied and it is disclosed here rather than passed off as layout-faithful. OPTIONS ARE THEIR OWN ROWS: item_text IS THE STEM ALONE. Corrected 2026-09-14 after the first version of this table concatenated the lettered options into item_text. This is the shape the schema provides for when the two differ: 'The item response data will have a scored response in the resp column in such cases while the item text will retain the categorical option in the resp_raw column.' Both resp AND raw_resp are populated here, because unlike the case the schema describes the key IS recoverable -- so the table gives the scored value, the categorical option and the key together rather than substituting one for another. The deposit sits behind Dataverse Guestbook 80, which returns HTTP 400 to every API route, so the files were obtained by a human answering the guestbook form in a browser -- the same wall and the same workaround as batch_202's gilbert_meta_73. TWO KINDS OF FILE ARE USED AND THEY CHECK EACH OTHER: (1) the student-assessment Stata files inside 'PSL Baseline and Midline Dataverse Files.zip' -- rawdata_public/baseline/student/SA_CLEAN_Master_deidentified.dta and rawdata_public/midline/final/Student Assessment/PSL_SA_deidentified_cleaned.dta -- whose VARIABLE LABELS are the item wording; and (2) the printed instruments 'Baseline Survey Tools.zip' -> PSL_Baseline_Student_Assessment.pdf and 'Midline Survey Tools.zip' -> PSL_midline_student_assessment_final_printable.pdf, which supply the section structure, the child-facing enumerator script, the listening-comprehension story texts, and an explicit CORRECT ANSWER line per item.
note: PARTIAL SHIP: 25 of 37 codes carry item_text, 12 do not. THE CENTRAL FINDING, AND THE REASON FOR THE BLANKS: THE ITEM CODES ARE FORM POSITIONS, NOT ITEMS. The study fielded two different test forms -- baseline and midline -- and the live table pools them into wave 0 and wave 1 under ONE set of item codes. Of the codes defined on both forms, almost all carry DIFFERENT CONTENT at the two waves. Concretely, in gilbert_meta_14 addition_q2 is '6 + 1 = 7' at baseline and '0 + 3 =' at midline (which is baseline's addition_q3), and wordprob1 and wordprob2 are simply SWAPPED between the two forms; in gilbert_meta_13 objectid1 is a picture of a book at baseline and a mouse at midline, and reading_level1_comp1 is 'What does John do?' against a farming passage at baseline but 'Where did the wild cat run?' against an entirely different passage at midline. So there is no single item_text for those codes, and shipping either form's wording would be wrong for every row from the other wave. item_text is left blank for exactly those codes and populated for every code whose content is unambiguous -- the form-exclusive ones plus wordprob5, which is identical on both forms. This is a partial ship in the same sense as socialstereotype_hughes_2025_judgement and gilbert_meta_45, except the limit is a property of the response table rather than of the sources: the sources are complete and excellent. WORTH RAISING ON THE DATA SIDE. Pooling two forms' contents under one item code is the kind of thing that breaks the IRW `item` contract, and it is invisible to anyone reading the response table -- addition_q2 looks like one item. It is the same class of defect as the oxfordcovid_xue_2024 filter bug (#1996) and deserves its own issue rather than being buried in an itemtext note; a wave-specific code (or item_family) would fix it and would make ~2/3 of these two tables' item text shippable. A SECOND, SMALLER REASON FOR BLANK item_text, AND IT IS NOT THE SAME REASON. The objectid_ and numdiscrim_ codes are handbook stimuli: the child is shown a picture (objectid) or a pair of printed numbers (numdiscrim) and must name the object or say which number is bigger. For those the variable label is the EXPECTED ANSWER, not a question stem -- 'Chair', '425 (Four hundred twenty-five)'. Putting that in item_text would misrepresent an answer key as the wording a child read, so it ships as correct_response with item_text blank, per the 2026-09-05 picture-stimulus ruling, and the section_prompt carries the instrument's own spoken task ('Now here are some more images. I want you to point to each image and tell me what it is.' / 'Now I will show you some numbers. I will point to two numbers at a time and I want you to tell me which number is bigger.'). verify_psl_common.R test 3 distinguishes the two reasons explicitly so the blank counts reconcile. ON THE ARITHMETIC ITEMS' APPEARANCE: the instrument is enumerator-facing, so the baseline form prints the problem WITH its answer ('12 + 6 = 18') for the enumerator to mark against while the child works it in the student handbook. item_text is that string verbatim rather than a reconstructed '12 + 6 = ___', because the standard's rule is to transcribe literally and disclose, not to normalise silently; correct_response repeats the answer so it is usable without parsing the stem. The midline form prints the problem without the answer ('0 + 3 =') and states the key separately, which is one more sign the two forms are different documents. A PDF EXTRACTION ARTIFACT, HANDLED: the printed instruments render every lowercase 'w' followed by a spurious space, so extracted text reads 'w ordprob1', 'How  many', 'Show  me'. item_text is therefore taken from the .dta variable labels, which are clean, and the PDFs are used only for keys, sections and prompts. The de-artifacted PDF text still agrees with the labels on 49 of 49 (gilbert_meta_13) and 109 of 109 (gilbert_meta_14) item-form pairs, which is what establishes that the labels are administered wording rather than internal shorthand. The section_prompt strings were transcribed by hand with the artifact corrected; that correction is the only normalisation applied to any shipped text. option_text is empty throughout: resp is a 0/1 correct/incorrect score, not which option was chosen. The midline form also offered a '-88 Don't Know' code, which the deposit's own 07b_Student_Prep_Midline.do recodes to 0, so it is absent from the live resp set and correctly absent here. The listening-comprehension story texts ARE in the baseline instrument and ship as section_prompt. Note that midline listening_quest3-5 are word-for-word the same three questions as baseline listening_comp4-6 and carry the same three keys (Kakata; lions, elephants and snakes; they share their meat), so the hunter-and-son story is attached to that midline section too -- an inference, but a well-supported one. The midline Level-1 listening story (about Paul and football) is NOT printed in the midline form, so that section carries the listening instruction without a story.

note: ITEM TEXT IS THE TASK, NOT A LITERAL ITEM, AND THAT IS INHERENT TO THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN A GAP. This is an ASER-family oral assessment: the printed tool shows a POOL of stimuli and instructs the enumerator to pick from it at random -- the baseline math sheet reads, in Hindi, 'ask them to read the digits below in order, then ask any 5 digits', and the two-digit identification task lists ten numbers of which any five are asked. So no fixed wording is a property of an item code, exactly as in gilbert_meta_70/71 in this same batch, and the honest text is the task. WHERE THE TEXT COMES FROM: the deposit's own variable labels in ml_merged.dta, verbatim except for stripping the leading question number ('q31 No. of 1to9 numbers Read' -> 'No. of 1to9 numbers Read'). The deposit's spelling is kept as found, including its 'substraction'. Nothing here is IRW prose. THE BASELINE LABELS ARE USED, NOT THE ENDLINE ONES, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE CHOICE WITH A PROOF BEHIND IT. The endline label set is shifted by one position: e_caser_math_add2 reads 'q39 single digit subtraction' and e_caser_math_subtr1 reads only 'Q39', leaving q38 unused and q39 duplicated. The administration cascade settles which is right -- add2 is given only to children who PASSED add1 (n matches add1's passers exactly at both waves), which a subtraction item would not be -- so the variable NAMES are correct and those two endline labels are a deposit typo. The baseline labels q36-q39 have no gaps or repeats and describe the same five arithmetic tasks the printed endline tool shows, so they are the text shipped for all nine both-wave codes; subtr3 is endline-only and takes its own endline label. WHY THE ITEM TEXT IS THE SAME AT BOTH WAVES HERE, UNLIKE THE PSL TABLES: the two forms differ only in the specific numerals printed on the sheet (baseline single-digit addition shows 5+4 and 9+4, endline shows 4+3 and 8+3), not in the task. Since item_text is the task, one value is correct for both waves. resp IS AN ALL-CORRECT INDICATOR, NOT A RAW SCORE, and that is not visible from the response table. The deposit scores the reading and identification items as COUNTS (digits 1-9 read out of 9; 11-20 read out of 10; five numbers identified in each of three ranges) and the arithmetic items as Yes/No/No-response. The live 0/1 is 1 only for a perfect count or a Yes. Reproduced on nine of ten items to within the ~6% analysis-sample restriction. correct_response is therefore empty: there is no single key, because the enumerator selects the stimuli, and resp already encodes accuracy. option_text is empty for the same reason. DEFECT TO REPORT ON THE DATA SIDE -- caser_math_read1. Its live resp corresponds to raw code 9, which is eight of nine digits read, not raw code 10, which is all nine; the pass rate is 1.3% where the correct dichotomisation gives 58-64%. read1 is also the only code carried for all 14,576 participants at both waves instead of the ~94% analysis sample, so its missing values appear to have been filled with 0. Both are upstream of this repo. Item text is unaffected and ships; the resp needs its own issue, as with oxfordcovid_xue_2024 (#1996). Anyone using read1 as-is will read a near-floor item that is not one. section_prompt carries the two task groups the printed tool uses (number reading and identification, then arithmetic); the tool's spoken instructions are printed in Devanagari in a legacy font that does not extract, and translating them myself would put IRW prose in a field defined as administered wording, so they are not shipped.
public_note: Ten numeracy items from the child ASER test used in a maternal-literacy evaluation in Bihar, administered at baseline (wave 0) and endline (wave 1). caser_math_subtr3, two-digit carry-over subtraction, was added at endline and appears at wave 1 only. ITEM TEXT IS THE TASK, NOT A FIXED QUESTION. This is an orally administered ASER-style test: the printed sheet shows a pool of numbers and problems and the enumerator picks from it -- 'ask any 5 digits' -- so no single wording belongs to an item code. The text given is the study's own description of each task, taken verbatim from its data files. The baseline and endline sheets print different numerals for the same tasks, so one description is correct for both waves. TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE MODELLING THIS TABLE. First, resp is an ALL-CORRECT indicator, not a raw score: the study scored the reading and identification items as counts (nine digits, ten numbers, five numbers in each range) and this table gives 1 only for a perfect count. Second, it is a CASCADING test -- a child attempted two-digit addition only after passing one-digit addition, and two-digit subtraction only after passing one-digit subtraction -- so the harder items have far fewer responses and their pass rates are conditional on an already-selected, more able group. Comparing raw item means across levels will mislead. KNOWN PROBLEM WITH ONE ITEM: caser_math_read1 (reading digits 1-9) appears to be dichotomised one step too low, giving a 1.3% pass rate where the study's own coding implies 58-64%, and it is the only item recorded for every participant at both waves rather than the analysis sample. Its item text is correct; treat its resp as unreliable pending a data fix. Verified by the study's own variable labels, by subtr3 appearing at exactly the wave its code list defines, and by the cascade: each follow-on item's respondent count equals its gate item's number of passers exactly at both waves.
